The two bunching wall exit laws are geometric with parameters f and b and share the same continuation H from (2,+1), or H=1 for N=2. Their PGF difference has numerator z(f-b)(1-z)H; the 1-z cancels for cumulative probabilities. The remaining product has nonnegative coefficients. For N>=3 a leftward run reaches w, using a reverse step first if needed; a right-facing walker at site 1 can first move to site 2 and reverse. H has a positive coefficient from a rightward run. For N=2 only w reaches w, and equality at f=b is of hitting laws, not of transition kernels. Positive probabilities of finite rightward runs give almost-sure absorption.
